'''Melat Asfawosen Kiros'''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/588655/Melat_Asfawosen_Kiros.html |title=Melat Kiros - D Colorado, 1st, Candidate |website=[[LegiStorm]] |access-date=August 24, 2026}}</ref> (born 1997)<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stein |first=Chris |date=July 1, 2026 |title=Democratic socialist Melat Kiros defeats 15-term incumbent in Colorado House primary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/01/melat-kiros-democrat-defeats-diana-degette-blue-state-colarado-house-primary-denver |access-date=July 2, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> is an American lawyer, graduate student, and politician.<ref name="Slevin-2026">{{Cite web|last1=Slevin|first1=Colleen |last2=Paul |first2=Jesse |date=June 26, 2026 |title=Melat Kiros may be on the verge of unseating Diana DeGette. Here's how that came to be. |url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/06/26/melat-kiros-diana-degette-race-colorado/ |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=The Colorado Sun |language=en-US}}</ref> A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and the [[Democratic Socialists of America]], she is the incoming [[United States House of Representatives|representative]] of [[Colorado's 1st congressional district]], defeating Republican Christy Peterson in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Colorado#District 1|2026 midterm elections]]. Kiros became the Democratic nominee after prevailing against 15-term incumbent [[Diana DeGette]] in the primary. Kiros supports [[Medicare for All]], [[Abolish ICE|abolishing ICE]], federal [[rent control]], and a [[Moratorium (law)|moratorium]] on [[data center]]s.

She is the first [[Generation Z]] woman elected to Congress and the second Generation Z member of Congress, after [[Maxwell Frost]].<ref name= "Moore-2026" /> She is also the first Black woman to represent Colorado in the House.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Hernandez |first=Esteban L. |date=November 4, 2026 |title=Melat Kiros easily wins 1st District seat |url=https://www.axios.com/local/denver/2026/11/04/melat-kiros-1st-district-seat-midterm-elections |access-date=November 4, 2026 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Kiros was born in [[Addis Ababa]], Ethiopia, to a family of [[Tigrayan]] origin, and her parents [[Immigration to the United States|immigrated to the United States]] when she was an infant.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hurwitz |first=Sophie |title=Gaza is costing Democratic incumbents their seats |url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2026/06/encampments-democratic-party-chris-rabb-melat-kiros-darializa-chevalier/ |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=Mother Jones |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name= "Denver Westword-2025">{{Cite web |date=August 12, 2025 |title=Meet the Gen Z Candidates Challenging Colorado's Longest-Serving Congressmember |url=https://www.westword.com/news/gen-z-candidates-challenge-longest-serving-colorado-congress-25259491/ |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=Denver Westword |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= Prokop |first= Andrew |title= Melat Kiros is the first political star truly formed by the 2020s |url= https://www.vox.com/politics/493863/melat-kiros-defeats-diana-degette-dsa-israel-gaza |website= [[Vox Media|Vox]] |date= July 1, 2026 |access-date= July 2, 2026 |archive-date= July 1, 2026 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260701142111/https://www.vox.com/politics/493863/melat-kiros-defeats-diana-degette-dsa-israel-gaza |url-status= live}}</ref> According to her campaign website, Kiros was born "weeks before" her father was picked in the United States' [[Diversity Visa Lottery]].<ref name= "Melat Kiros for Congress">{{Cite web |title= About |url= https://www.kirosforco.com/about |access-date= July 1, 2026 |website= Melat Kiros for Congress |language= en}}</ref>

Kiros grew up in [[Aurora, Colorado]],<ref name="Melat Kiros for Congress"/><ref name=PhD>{{Cite web |title= Meet Our PhD Students: Melat Kiros|url= https://publicaffairs.ucdenver.edu/people/meet-our-phd-students#ac-melat-kiros-9 |access-date= July 1, 2026 |website= CU Denver Public Affairs |language= en}}</ref> and attended [[Eaglecrest High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |title= Fact Sheet |url= https://www.kirosforco.com/fact-sheet |access-date= July 1, 2026 |website= Melat Kiros for Congress |language= en}}</ref> She graduated from [[Washington College]] with a bachelor's degree in political science and economics in 2018, and from [[Notre Dame Law School]] in 2022.<ref name=PhD/><ref name= "Schartz-2026">{{Cite news |last= Schartz |first= Emma |last2= Salhotra |first2= Pooja |date=June 29, 2026 |title= 'No One's Coming to Save Us but Us': Gen Z Runs for Office |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/29/us/elections/colorado-primary-gen-z.html |access-date= June 30, 2026 |work= The New York Times |language= en-US |issn= 0362-4331}}</ref>

==Early career==
Kiros joined the New York law office of [[Sidley Austin]] as a summer associate in 2021, becoming a full-time associate in September 2022. At the time of her firing she was a securities regulatory and enforcement associate.<ref name="law">{{cite news |last1= Nair |first1= Krishnan |title= Sidley Fires Associate After She Speaks Out Against Law Firms' Letter on Antisemitism |url= https://www.law.com/americanlawyer/2023/11/13/sidley-fires-associate-after-she-speaks-out-against-law-firms-letter-on-israel-gaza-405-131883/ |access-date= 13 February 2026 |publisher= [[Law.com]] |date= 13 November 2023}}</ref><ref name= "Schartz-2026" /><ref name= "Reuters">{{Cite news |title= Divisions mount over US law firms' response to Israel-Hamas war |url= https://www.reuters.com/legal/legalindustry/divisions-mount-over-us-law-firms-response-israel-hamas-war-2023-11-14/ |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240614081748/https://www.reuters.com/legal/legalindustry/divisions-mount-over-us-law-firms-response-israel-hamas-war-2023-11-14/ |archive-date= June 14, 2024 |access-date= July 1, 2026 |work= [[Reuters]] |language= en-US}}</ref> In 2023, she published a post on [[Medium (website)|Medium]] criticizing law firms, including her own, for opposing [[Gaza war protests in the United States|pro-Palestine protests]] and highlighting the "chilling future" of lawyers' employment prospects for criticism of the Israeli government's actions and its legitimacy."<ref>{{Cite web |last= Lacy |first= Akela |date= December 4, 2025 |title= She Lost Her Job for Speaking Out About Gaza. Can It Power Her to Congress? |url= https://theintercept.com/2025/12/04/denver-primary-melat-kiros-diana-degette-justice-democrats/ |access-date= July 1, 2026 |website= The Intercept |language= en-US}}</ref><ref name="Reuters" /> Sidley Austin asked Kiros to take the letter down. When she refused, she was fired.<ref>{{Cite news |last= Wang |first= Philip |date= July 1, 2026 |title= Meet Melat Kiros, the Democratic Socialist Who Won Colorado's Primary |url= https://time.com/article/2026/06/30/melat-kiros-democratic-socialist-colorado-congressional-race/ |access-date= July 2, 2026 |work= Time |language= en-US |issn= 0040-781X}}</ref>

After leaving Sidley Austin, Kiros returned to Colorado, enrolled in a PhD program at the [[University of Colorado Denver School of Public Affairs]], studying "the efficacy of reparations, universal basic income and regulatory reform in achieving social, economic, and environmental equity."<ref name= PhD/> She worked as a [[barista]] to help pay off her student loans.<ref name= "Denver Westword-2025" /><ref name="Yahoo News-2026">{{Cite web |date= July 1, 2026 |title= Who is Melat Kiros — the Democratic Socialist who unseated a nearly 30-year incumbent representing Denver in Congress? |url= https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/melat-kiros-democratic-socialist-unseated-034628047.html |access-date= July 1, 2026 |website= 9News |language= en-US|last=Baitinger|first=Brooke|via=Yahoo News}}</ref>

On July 9, 2025, Kiros announced her candidacy for the [[United States House of Representatives]] for [[Colorado's 1st congressional district]], challenging incumbent [[Diana DeGette]], who was first elected to Congress in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Luning |first= Ernest |date=July 10, 2025 |title=Denver Democrat Diana DeGette draws primary challenge, call for 'new generation' from Melat Kiros |url=https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2025/07/09/denver-democrat-diana-degette-draws-primary-challenge-call-for-new-generation-from-melat-kiros-fa6c7d97-e15d-4a61-823b-f483222ccbea/ |access-date=July 1, 2026 |website=Colorado Politics |language=en-US}}</ref>

When asked about her motivation for challenging DeGette, who is widely considered to be on the progressive side of the Democratic Party, Kiros signaled that the campaign would focus on the generational divide, as well as money in politics. Kiros has refused donations from corporate PACs and special interest groups in her campaign. She went on to criticize over $5 million in corporate PAC money that DeGette had received from the [[pharmaceutical lobby]] and the [[fossil fuels lobby]].<ref name="salon">{{cite news |last1= Payne |first1= Russell |date= 15 December 2025 |title= Progressive bid tests Democratic unity in Colorado's First District |url= https://www.salon.com/2025/12/15/progressive-bid-tests-democratic-unity-in-colorados-first-district/ |access-date= 15 February 2026 |publisher=[[Salon.com|Salon]]}}</ref>

During the primary, Kiros was endorsed by [[Justice Democrats]], the [[Democratic Socialists of America]], the [[Working Families Party]], and U.S. Senator [[Bernie Sanders]].<ref name= "Slevin-2026"/><ref>{{Cite web |last= Panetta|first= Grace |date= June 30, 2026 |title= A 29-Year-Old Democratic Socialist Takes on Colorado's Most Senior Member of Congress |url= https://talkingpointsmemo.com/news/a-29-year-old-democratic-socialist-takes-on-colorados-most-senior-member-of-congress |access-date= July 1, 2026 |website= Talking Points Memo |language= en-US}}</ref> DeGette was endorsed by the [[Congressional Progressive Caucus]].<ref>{{Cite web |date= June 29, 2026 |title= Colorado Democrats brace for their own insurgent earthquake |url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/29/bennet-degette-colorado-primaries-progressives-00979355 |access-date= July 1, 2026 |website= Politico |language= en}}</ref>

''[[The Colorado Sun]]'' reported that the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]] was the biggest policy difference between Kiros and DeGette. Kiros supports an embargo on all arms sales to Israel, and says that Israel should no longer be a [[Jewish state]], calling it an [[ethnocracy]].<ref name="Slevin-2026" />

The primary campaign saw large amounts of outside spending, primarily supporting DeGette and attacking Kiros.<ref name="Slevin-2026"/> Three [[Super PAC]]s spent $1.3 million on advertisements attacking Kiros in the campaign's last two months.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paul |first=Jesse |date=June 19, 2026 |title=Super PACs drop $1.3M in last-minute spree to protect Diana DeGette in Denver's congressional district |url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/06/19/diana-degette-melat-kiros-pac-spending/|access-date=July 1, 2026 |website=The Colorado Sun |language=en-US}}</ref> Kiros won the primary on June 30 by over 20,000 votes; her victory garnered national attention and was described as an "upset" that highlighted the growing influence of anti-establishment and DSA-aligned candidates.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hernandez |first=Esteban L. |date=2026-07-01 |title=Kiros ousts 15-term Colorado U.S. Rep. DeGette |url=https://www.axios.com/local/denver/2026/07/01/colorado-primary-results-melat-kiros-beats-diana-degette |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6193380-kiros-wins-colorado-house-seat/|title=Melat Kiros wins Colorado House seat after ousting Diana DeGette in primary|first=Sudiksha|last=Kochi|date=November 4, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bedayn |first=-Jesse |last2=Bedayn |first2=Associated Press Jesse |last3=Press |first3=Associated |date=2026-07-01 |title=Democratic socialist Melat Kiros defeats longtime House incumbent in Colorado primary |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democratic-socialist-melat-kiros-defeats-longtime-house-incumbent-in-colorado-primary |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=PBS News |language=en-us}}</ref>

The district is so heavily Democratic that Kiros was overwhelmingly favored to win the general election.<ref name="Moore-2026">{{Cite news |last=Moore |first=Elena |date=July 1, 2026 |title=Democratic socialist Melat Kiros poised to become the first Gen Z woman in Congress |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/07/01/nx-s1-5876122/colorado-primary-election-melat-kiros-democratic-socialist |access-date= July 1, 2026 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref> On November 3, she was elected with 78.3% of the vote,<ref>{{Cite web |last= Hernandez |first= Esteban L. |date= 2026-11-04 |title= Melat Kiros easily wins 1st District seat |url= https://www.axios.com/local/denver/2026/11/04/melat-kiros-1st-district-seat-midterm-elections |access-date= 2026-11-04 |website= Axios |language= en}}</ref> becoming the first [[Generation Z]] woman elected to Congress and the second Generation Z member of Congress, after [[Maxwell Frost]].<ref name= "Moore-2026" /> She is also the first Black woman to represent Colorado in the House.<ref name="auto"/>

== Political positions ==
Kiros is a [[democratic socialist]]. She has pledged to refuse corporate [[political action committee]] (PAC) donations.<ref name="Yahoo News-2026" />

=== Economic policy ===
[[File:Melat Kiros for Congress logo.png|thumb|2026 congressional campaign logo]]
Kiros supports expanding public social programs in light of market disruption caused by [[artificial intelligence]] and automation.<ref name="Dolven-2026">{{Cite web |last=Dolven |first=Taylor |date=May 29, 2026 |title=Where Diana DeGette, Melat Kiros and Wanda James stand on the issues in Colorado's 1st Congressional District primary |url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/05/29/diana-degette-melat-kiros-wanda-james-colorado-primary-election-issue-guide/ |access-date=July 1, 2026 |website=The Colorado Sun |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Yahoo News-2026" />

Kiros supports raising the federal minimum wage to match local living costs, with a floor of at least $15 per hour, and has said it may need to be $22 per hour in some cities or districts.<ref name="Dolven-2026" /> She supports closing [[tax loopholes]] and higher taxes on the "ultra wealthy".<ref name="Dolven-2026" />

On housing policy, Kiros supports upzoning and permitting reform, federal rent control, and [[social housing]].<ref name="Dolven-2026" />

=== Environmental policy ===
Kiros supports a [[Green New Deal]] and argues that transportation policy should emphasize [[public transport]] and pedestrian-centered neighborhoods rather than relying mainly on electric vehicles.<ref name= "Dolven-2026" /> She supports a moratorium on [[data center]]s until federal labor and environmental regulations are in place, and said data-center companies should generate their own renewable energy.<ref name="Dolven-2026" />

=== Foreign policy ===
Kiros supports a 10% reduction in Pentagon spending, arguing that reducing the [[military budget]] would decrease incentives for defense contractors and the [[military-industrial complex]] to support war.<ref name= "Dolven-2026" /><ref name="DeMare-2026">{{Cite web |last=DeMare |first= Kiara |date=May 18, 2026 |title= Melat Kiros says she'll bring change, lower costs in bid for Congressional District 1 seat |url= https://www.cpr.org/2026/05/18/cd-1-race-melat-kiros-democrat-interview/ |access-date=July 1, 2026 |website= Colorado Public Radio |language=en}}</ref> She opposes continued [[U.S. military aid to Israel]], calling [[Gaza genocide|Israel's actions in Gaza a genocide]], and has called for a full U.S. [[arms embargo]] on Israel, including defensive weapons.<ref name="Dolven-2026" /><ref name="Prokop-2026" /><ref>{{Cite web |title= Democratic socialist Melat Kiros defeats incumbent Diana DeGette in Colorado House primary |url= https://www.reuters.com/world/us/democratic-socialist-melat-kiros-defeats-incumbent-diana-degette-colorado-house-2026-07-01/|access-date=July 3, 2026|date=June 30, 2026 |work=[[Reuters]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Kiros opposed [[2026 Iran war|U.S. military action against Iran]], saying there was no security threat, and no indication that Iran was close to building [[Iranian nuclear program|nuclear weapons]]. She said she would support efforts to reclaim [[War Powers Clause|Congressional war powers]] from the president.<ref name="Dolven-2026" /><ref name="DeMare-2026" />

In September 2026, Kiros attended a protest ahead of a speech by Israeli prime minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] at the [[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|United Nations General Assembly]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Speri |first=Alice |last2=McMenamin |first2=Lex |date=September 24, 2026 |title= Netanyahu's speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: 'Let Gaza live' |url= https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/24/netanyahu-un-protests |access-date= September 25, 2026 |work= The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

=== Healthcare and childcare ===
Kiros supports [[Medicare for All]], cancellation of [[medical debt]], federal drug-price caps, and breaking up monopolies in the [[Pharmaceutical industry|pharmaceutical]], [[Health insurance industry|health insurance]], and [[Healthcare industry|health-care]] provider sectors.<ref name="Dolven-2026" /><ref name= "Prokop-2026">{{Cite web |last=Prokop |first=Andrew |date=June 24, 2026 |title=The Democratic Tea Party is here. Here's where it might go next. |url=https://www.vox.com/politics/492225/colorado-primaries-melat-kiros-julie-gonzales-hickenlooper-degette |access-date=July 1, 2026 |website=Vox |language=en}}</ref> She supports increased childcare subsidies, capping childcare costs at 10% of family income, and making childcare free for families below a certain income level.<ref name= "Dolven-2026" />

=== Immigration ===
Kiros supports hiring more [[immigration judge]]s, caseworkers, and border-processing staff to make the immigration system faster. She supports abolishing [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] and releasing people without criminal records from ICE detention.<ref name="Dolven-2026" />
